text.p: Panama's Congress approved a 1997 government budget of $4.728 billion, up 0.38 percent over the 1996 budget, which was $4.710 billion.
In a 41-16 vote, lawmakers approved the budget late on Monday. The budget will take effect from January 1, according to a statement from the congressional press office.
Some $1.1 billion is earmarked for social spending to build roads, hospitals and schools.
Debt service payments will amount to $812 million, including $364 million in interest and $447 million in principle payments.
Panama completed its Brady bond debt restructuring package in July by issuing bonds in exchange for $3.5 billion of medium and long-term commercial debt.
The financial instruments that were exchanged involved around $2 biliion in principle and $1.5 billion in past due interest of Panama's external debt owed to private creditors.
